title: Weekly In-Class Activities
text:
ECN 4199 — Weekly In-Class Activities
This page contains the weekly in-class activities for ECN 4199: Industrial Data Analytics.
Each activity must be completed during the scheduled lecture hour.



Assessment Structure



Item
Details




Number of Activities
13


Marks per Activity
5 marks


Total Marks
65 marks


Duration
1 hour per activity


Access
Lecturer passcode required


Submission
Through weekly submission link


Completion Time
During lecture only






Important Instructions
Students must:

Attend the scheduled lecture.
Wait until the lecturer announces the passcode.
Open the relevant weekly activity.
Complete the activity within one hour.
Submit before the activity closes.

Late submissions will not be accepted unless approved by the lecturer.



How Activities Work
Each weekly activity may include:

short conceptual questions
Python coding tasks
interpretation questions
graph or output interpretation
short reflection questions

The purpose is not memorisation.
The purpose is to test whether students can apply the weekly concepts in real time.



Passcode Access
Each activity will be protected by a lecturer-set passcode.
The passcode will be announced only during the relevant lecture.
Students should not share passcodes with others.



Weekly Activity Table



Week
Topic
Marks
Duration
Activity Link




Week 1
Orientation and First Python Code
5
1 hour
Open Activity







Submission Format
Each activity must be submitted through the relevant weekly activity link.
Where a Colab notebook is required, students must:

Save a copy in Google Drive.
Rename the notebook properly.
Set sharing to:

Anyone with the link → Viewer

Submit the notebook link.




Notebook Naming Convention
Use the following format:
WeekNumber_IndexNumber_Name.ipynb
Example:
Week05_2024BA12345_Perera.ipynb



Marking
Each weekly activity is worth 5 marks.
The total mark across all 13 activities is:
13 × 5 = 65 marks
Marks will be based on:



Component
Marks




Correct completion of required task
2


Correct code/output
1


Economic interpretation
1


Timely submission and formatting
1


Total
5






Academic Integrity
Students may use course materials and lecture notebooks.
However:

copying another student’s work is not allowed
submitting work without understanding is not allowed
AI tools must not be used to replace student reasoning
all submitted explanations must be written in the student’s own words




Lecturer Note
The weekly links will be activated or shared during the relevant lecture period only.

title: ECN 4199 — Industrial Data Analytics
text:
Welcome to the course website for ECN 4199: Industrial Data Analytics.
This course introduces students to modern computational and analytical tools increasingly used in:

economics
business analytics
policy analysis
finance
industry research
AI-assisted decision systems

The course is specifically designed for students with little or no prior programming experience.
You are not expected to become a computer scientist.
You are expected to become an economist who can:

work confidently with data
think computationally
interpret analytical outputs critically
communicate evidence effectively
use AI systems responsibly

title: Week 1 — Orientation: Python, AI, and Data Analytics
text:
Welcome to ECN 4199 — Industrial Data Analytics.
This week is not about advanced coding. It is about removing fear, understanding the course workflow, and running your first Python code.

title: Week 1 — Orientation: Python, AI, and Data Analytics
text:
Formula
GDP Growth = [(GDP this year - GDP last year) / GDP last year] × 100

title: Week 1 — Orientation: Python, AI, and Data Analytics
text:
Python code
gdp_last_year = 1000
gdp_this_year = 1080

gdp_growth = ((gdp_this_year - gdp_last_year) / gdp_last_year) * 100

print(gdp_growth)

title: Week 1 — Orientation: Python, AI, and Data Analytics
text:
Interpretation
The economy grew by 8 percent.

title: Week 1 — Orientation: Python, AI, and Data Analytics
text:
Formula
Inflation Rate = [(CPI this year - CPI last year) / CPI last year] × 100

title: Week 1 — Orientation: Python, AI, and Data Analytics
text:
Python code
cpi_last_year = 200
cpi_this_year = 240

inflation_rate = ((cpi_this_year - cpi_last_year) / cpi_last_year) * 100

print(inflation_rate)

title: Week 1 — Orientation: Python, AI, and Data Analytics
text:
Interpretation
Prices increased by 20 percent.

title: Week 1 — Orientation: Python, AI, and Data Analytics
text:
Formula
Depreciation = [(New exchange rate - Old exchange rate) / Old exchange rate] × 100

title: Week 1 — Orientation: Python, AI, and Data Analytics
text:
Python code
exchange_rate_old = 320
exchange_rate_new = 360

depreciation = ((exchange_rate_new - exchange_rate_old) / exchange_rate_old) * 100

print(depreciation)

title: Week 1 — Orientation: Python, AI, and Data Analytics
text:
Interpretation
The domestic currency depreciated by 12.5 percent.

title: Week 1 — Orientation: Python, AI, and Data Analytics
text:
Formula
Real Income = Nominal Income / Price Index × 100

title: Week 1 — Orientation: Python, AI, and Data Analytics
text:
Python code
nominal_income = 100000
price_index = 125

real_income = (nominal_income / price_index) * 100

print(real_income)

title: Week 1 — Orientation: Python, AI, and Data Analytics
text:
Interpretation
Although nominal income is 100,000, real income is 80,000 in base-year prices.
